title: eraseFromPlay files an erased unit under its owner, but zones follow control
summary: E.eraseFromPlay emits its 'erased' event with seat: u.owner, so a stolen unit erased from play (e.g. as a cost) is filed on its OWNER's erased pile. The owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“zones follow control, in all four…”) rules that zones follow control in all four per-seat destinations, and supersession.json corrects the owner ruling of 2026-08-25 (“an ERASE is a despawn; the…”) item 3 (the erased-from-play seat) by the owner ruling of 2026-08-30 (“zones follow control, in all four…”) accordingly. The Unstable-death erase route already uses the controller (binSeat = opts.binTo ?? u.controller), so only this route differs. Found in Stage B4.

evidence.quote: unit: u.id, card: u.card, seat: u.owner, region: u.region,
// CR 410.4b: the host AND its mods reach the public erased pile, under the
zones follow control, in all four of them

title: The Electric glossary row still says excess is lost at the end of the chain
summary: ui/glossary.ts's {Electric} row (cites the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Electric damage pathing […]”) only) says each unit absorbs only enough to die and 'When the chain runs out the excess is lost'. The owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“{Electric}'s jump is optional, and excess…”) (amending the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Electric damage pathing […]”)) rules each hop optional (excess may stay on the current unit) and a dead-end remainder is dealt to the last unit, never lost; the owner ruling of 2026-10-10 (“{Piercing} is elective outside combat too […]”) makes the Piercing dead end elective. The row's text states superseded law; its text was left alone (B3 changes headings only).

evidence.quote: When the chain runs out the excess is lost — unless the source is also {Piercing}, which sends it to that unit’s controller.
no {Piercing} is read: it stays on the last unit — dealt, never lost
